headline: Verstappen masters the wet to win in Kuala Lumpur
standfirst: Max Verstappen won the Bahrain Grand Prix for Red Bull Racing, finishing 2.307s ahead of Kimi Antonelli, with Lewis Hamilton completing the podium after 55 laps of Kuala Lumpur.

sections.title: The start
sections.body: Max Verstappen lined up first on the grid. Verstappen converted that into the lead at the end of lap one.

sections.title: How it unfolded
sections.body: The lead changed hands 5 times. Laps led: Verstappen (43), Antonelli (11) and Piastri (1). Verstappen took the lead for good on lap 45. The race was neutralised by 2 safety car periods (lap 9–12, 45–51).

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Verstappen made 3 stops, running intermediate → soft tyres. The field made 73 pit stops in total; the quickest stationary time was 2.1s for Colapinto on lap 31.

sections.title: Movers
sections.body: Arvid Lindblad made up the most ground, climbing 12 places from 22nd to 10th. Bortoleto went the other way, slipping from 10th to 18th. Timing recorded 505 on-track position changes, 36 of them by Hulkenberg.

sections.title: Retirements
sections.body: Russell (lap 50), Albon (lap 42) and Bottas (lap 8) failed to finish.

sections.title: Conditions and pace
sections.body: A damp track called for wet-weather tyres for part of the distance, although little rain fell during the race itself. Track temperature ranged from 33°C to 34°C, with air at 26–28°C. Max Verstappen set the fastest lap, a 1:38.220 on lap 55.
